description: Ekibimizle birlikte Nasa Space App Challangeye bu yıl üçüncü kez başvuruda bulunacağız. Her yıl yeni deneyimler edinerek kendimizi geliştiriyoruz.
summary:
ESE Audio (Earth Sound Engine) is a web-based data sonification application that converts color intensity and temporal changes in NASA’s satellite and scientific map layers into a real-time audio stream and dynamic musical tempo.
Since fundamental climate data on our planet—such as precipitation, temperature, and aerosols—are typically presented through complex visual maps, it is difficult for the general public to intuitively perceive environmental changes over long time periods. ESE Audio analyzes scientific map layers retrieved via NASA GIBS (WMS) on a 2D map and a Three.js-based 3D globe, dynamically adjusting the playback speed of layer-specific musical themes based on data density. This allows users not only to examine climate changes on the planet through visual representations but also to track the intensity of these changes by hearing them directly.
details:
Project Objective and Operating Principle

ESE Audio converts scientific Earth observation data obtained from NASA from visual to audio, enabling users to track global changes both visually and aurally. The user selects the scientific layer and time range (1 day, 7 days, 14 days, or 30 days) from the left panel; while viewing the data on a flat map or an interactive 3D globe in the center of the screen, they manage the music theme and track the real-time speed multiplier from the right panel.

The fundamental analysis and sonification methods underlying the system are as follows:

Average Color Analysis: To prevent instantaneous noise and deviations in a single pixel, the average of the overall color distribution within the Earth disk is calculated in real time via HTML5 Canvas.

Layer-Specific Speed Profile and RedMap Calibration: Different color-to-speed rules, compatible with the scientific color scale, have been defined for each of the precipitation, temperature, and aerosol layers. Specifically, for critical layers such as precipitation, minimum–maximum threshold values (RedMap calibration) are set for the red color channel to ensure that the music speed multiplier increases directly as data density rises; in other layers, a smoothing algorithm is applied to maintain listening fluidity.

Time Series and Layer Tour: Selected 1-, 7-, 14-, or 30-day time series are played frame by frame to sonify temporal changes. Additionally, the Layer Tour feature automatically cycles through different NASA layers in sequence, providing a seamless stream that allows different data sets to be listened to one after another.

Dynamic Audio Backing: Each scientific layer is paired with a royalty-free musical theme (MP3) suited to its character. As data density changes, the playback speed of the music is updated in real time. If desired, users can use the “Select Music” feature to assign a single musical theme to all layers.

Benefits for Users and Science Communication

Since the human ear is extremely sensitive to changes in rhythm and tempo, weekly or monthly climate fluctuations can be easily detected without having to read complex graphs.

The ability to switch between 2D map and 3D globe modes provides an interactive exploration and presentation environment for both students and researchers.

Technologies and Data Sources Used

Data Sources and Reference Platforms: Scientific map layers were retrieved via NASA GIBS (WMS); NASA Worldview was used for layer validation and visual comparisons, and NASA Eyes on the Earth was used as a reference for live/interactive views of the Earth.

Front End and Graphics Engine: The interface and control panels were designed using HTML5 and CSS3 with a focus on a dark theme. The application’s data retrieval, color analysis, speed control, and layer tour algorithms were developed using JavaScript; the HTML5 Canvas API was used for image processing, and the Three.js engine was used for interactive 3D globe visualization.

Runtime Environment: To ensure high-performance data streaming without being hindered by browser security restrictions (CORS), we configured the project to run on a local server (Baslat.bat).
